CVE-2026-55465.title: Goobi viewer: Solr injection via unvalidated region parameter in spatial search
CVE-2026-55465.description: The Goobi viewer is a web application that allows digitised material to be displayed in a web browser. From version 22.04 to before version 26.05, the unauthenticated REST endpoint GET /api/v1/index/{solrField}/spatial/search concatenates the user-supplied region query parameter directly into a Solr query string with no escaping, no local-param stripping, and no runtime schema enforcement (the OpenAPI @Schema(pattern=...) annotation is documentation-only at the JAX-RS layer). An attacker can inject Solr local-param syntax ({!parent ...}, {!join ...}) and boolean operators to make access-restricted georeferenced records match the query, bypassing the access-condition filter. This issue has been patched in version 26.05.

net/sched: cls_flower: avoid stale mask references after delete

Flower releases a mask reference when a filter is removed from the
classifier. The filter object can remain alive while dump, walk, or
hardware reoffload paths hold a reference to it. Those paths can then
dereference f->mask after the mask has already been released.

Release the mask synchronously from the final __fl_put() while the caller
still holds the tcf_proto reference, and leave the existing RCU work to
free the mask. This keeps the mask available to every reader that still

CVE-2026-99762.title: batman-adv: mcast: validate tracker padding before forwarding
CVE-2026-99762.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: mcast: validate tracker padding before forwarding

A multicast tracker with an even number of destinations needs two
padding bytes after its destination list. batadv_mcast_forw_packet()
currently only checks that the count field and the addresses fit in
the tracker TVLV.

If an unpadded even tracker is compacted to an odd number of
destinations, batadv_mcast_forw_shrink_update_headers() includes those
missing padding bytes in the amount to remove. The subsequent memmove
can then write two bytes past the old packet tail. With no tailroom,
this corrupts skb_shared_info.

Include the required padding in the existing tracker length check.
This rejects the malformed tracker before either received or locally
generated packets can reach the compactor.
